    AI Overview
    An Ayatollah is a high-ranking title for Twelver Shia clergy, specializing in Islamic studies, jurisprudence, and theology
    . The title denotes significant religious authority and expertise, commonly used in Iran. Historically, this title is associated with key political leaders, including Ruhollah Khomeini and Ali Khamenei, who served as Supreme Leaders of Iran. 
    Key figures and recent developments regarding this title include: 
    • Ali Khamenei: Served as Iran’s Supreme Leader from 1989 until his death on February 28, 2026, holding ultimate religious and political authority [3, The New York Times].
    • Mojtaba Khamenei: Son of Ali Khamenei, he is a prominent cleric and a leading candidate for succession as Supreme Leader.
    • The Title:
      It is typically given to Shia scholars when their teachers and peers recognize their expertise in seminaries, often in Qom.
    • Role: Beyond religious leadership, Ayatollahs in Iran play critical roles in the nation’s political structure, particularly through the Assembly of Experts, which selects the Supreme Leader. 
    The term literally translates to "Sign of God" or "Sign of Allah".

    What does Ayatollah mean?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    An Ayatollah is a high-ranking, senior Shiite Muslim cleric recognized as an expert in Islamic studies, law, and jurisprudence. The term translates from Persian/Arabic as "Sign of God" (āyat allāh). These scholars are considered masters of religious law (sharia) and often serve as community leaders, with the most senior holding the title of Grand Ayatollah. 
    Key Details Regarding the Term Ayatollah: 
    • Role & Authority: Ayatollahs provide legal interpretation (fatwas) and religious guidance, particularly in Iran, Iraq, and other areas with significant Shia populations.
    • Clerical Hierarchy:
      It is a senior, but not the highest, rank in the Shia system. It is generally achieved after years of advanced study in seminaries (hawza), particularly studying Dars-e-Kharej.
    • Etymology: The title means "sign of God" or "miracle of Allah".
    • Origin: The title became commonly used in the early 20th century, though it was bestowed on some scholars earlier. 
    Usage Examples & Context: 
    • Ayatollah Ali Khamenei: The current Supreme Leader of Iran.
    • Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini: The leader of the 1979 Iranian Revolution.
    • Grand Ayatollah Ali al-Sistani: A prominent senior religious leader in Iraq. 
    Synonyms & Related Terms: 
    • Sign of God: Literal translation.
    • High-ranking Shiite Cleric/Scholar: Descriptive title.
    • Mujtahid: A scholar recognized for having the capacity for independent interpretation of Islamic law.
    • Marja-e-Taqlid (or Marja): "Source of Emulation," which refers specifically to Grand Ayatollahs whom ordinary Shia Muslims follow. 
    Note: In modern times, particularly post-1979 in Iran, many theologians who complete the final level of seminary studies are referred to as Ayatollahs, leading to a higher number of individuals holding the title than in previous centuries, as noted in Wikipedia's article on Ayatollah.

      Ayatollah is a title for high-ranking Twelver Shia clergy. It came into widespread usage in the 20th century. Those who hold this title must be men and specialists in Islamic sciences such as jurisprudence and principles, often teaching in seminaries. The next lower rank among these clergy is Hojjatoleslam.
